data.narrative:
Andrenam, a Series A defense and security company founded by Matej Cernosek and Alex Chu, has raised $18M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 companies (2 public, 8 private) in the same sector and stage, including Stark Defence, Singularity, NODA AI, Anduril Industries, and Helsing.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $18M raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, implying a $36M valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Stark Defence ($4.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M)—yields a median valuation of $400M, with a range of $125M to $4.0B. The wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity within early-stage defense tech valuations.

Triangulating these methods produces a range of $31M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $218M. The substantial spread reflects genuine uncertainty in stage-comparable valuation; peer multiples vary by over 30x. The low-end estimate assumes stage-progression mechanics dominate; the high end reflects outlier peer benchmarking. Key sensitivities include deal terms, revenue or customer traction not captured in the provided data, and relative positioning versus the Stark Defence outlier.
